articles.title: High-Resolution Model Developed for Tile-Drained Farm Fields
articles.summary: A new high-resolution model has been developed by researchers at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign to better understand how water moves through agricultural fields with tile drainage systems.
articles.content: A new study has shed light on how water behaves in tile-drained farm fields, a crucial aspect of modern agriculture that significantly impacts crop growth, nutrient transport, and water quality. However, despite its importance, modeling this complex process remains a challenge due to the numerous factors involved. Researchers at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign have developed a new high-resolution model to better understand how water moves through agricultural fields with tile drainage systems. The team used two test sites located on the university's Energy Farm to evaluate their model's performance and accuracy. The study focuses on the critical differences in soil, topography, and tile design that can greatly affect the way water behaves within a field. Most current models fail to capture these variations at a detailed level. Bin Peng, lead author of the study, explained that their new model provides an in-depth three-dimensional view of how water moves across the surface and through the soil after heavy rainfall events. This information is essential for farmers and policymakers who need to make informed decisions about agricultural practices and resource management. The research team worked closely with collaborators at Oak Ridge National Laboratory to incorporate detailed maps of tile locations into their model, allowing them to test its effectiveness in real-world scenarios. The model's ability to simulate real-world scenarios was enhanced by incorporating detailed maps of tile locations into its framework, a collaborative effort between researchers at various national laboratories. By testing two approaches for representing tile drainage in the Advanced Terrestrial Simulator, the team discovered that both methods produced reasonably accurate results at the field scale. However, each approach had its own advantages and limitations depending on the specific research question being addressed. One of the study's most striking findings was that simulations with varying resolutions, from 2 to 40 meters, yielded similar estimates of overall field-scale drainage once certain parameters were adjusted. This suggests that researchers may not necessarily require high-resolution models to estimate broad hydrological patterns. According to first author Haoyuan Yu, even at a resolution as coarse as 40 meters, the model was able to reproduce the overall tile-drainage response with reasonable accuracy. However, when examining spatial patterns, significant differences emerged between the two resolutions. The results indicate that while finer resolution is not always necessary for estimating overall field drainage or water-table response, it becomes increasingly important for understanding more nuanced aspects of water movement through soil and into the tile network. Field characteristics and drainage design significantly impact water pathways in tile-drained farm fields, influencing where water accumulates and interacts with its surroundings. Small variations in surface topography can affect where water ponded and entered the soil, while soil properties play a crucial role in balancing runoff, evapotranspiration, and tile drainage. This subtle interplay of factors underscores the complexity of hydrological pathways in these fields. Drain depth has a more pronounced impact on long-term cumulative drainage and water-table levels than other factors. Generally, deeper drains lower the water table and increase cumulative drainage, whereas shallower drains have less influence on these outcomes. A critical finding from this study is that tile spacing can significantly alter how quickly the drainage system responds to rainfall events. Closer spacing of tiles typically produces stronger peak drainage responses, which is an important consideration for farmers looking to optimize their drainage systems. The model's ability to test different tile locations, depths, and spacings allows researchers to predict and mitigate potential issues with ponding and water-table conditions before making any changes in the field. This approach can also inform strategies for managing dissolved nutrients, such as nitrate, which is highly soluble in water and moves through soil and drainage systems in tandem with water. Researchers are expanding a hydrological framework to account for carbon and nitrogen cycling as well as reactive transport processes. The enhanced model will allow scientists to compare water and nitrogen budgets of various bioenergy crops with those of traditional corn-soybean rotation systems. By doing so, they can identify more efficient and sustainable agricultural practices. This approach is expected to inform landscape design decisions for the bioeconomy. The ultimate goal of this project is to create a comprehensive digital model that simulates integrated surface-subsurface processes across vast agricultural landscapes. This digital twin will enable precision conservation and sustainable land management strategies. The research aims to guide landscape design decisions for the bioeconomy, sustainable land management, and precision conservation. By developing a field-to-watershed digital model, scientists can optimize water use and nutrient cycling in tile-drained farm fields, ultimately reducing environmental impacts and improving crop yields. articles.title: Himalayan Landslide Sends Shockwaves Through Region
articles.summary: A massive landslide occurred in the Himalayas on August 26, 2026, triggering an avalanche towards the Nepal-Tibet border.
articles.content: A massive landslide in the Himalayas has shaken the region, sending shockwaves that were initially mistaken for an earthquake. On August 26, 2026, a colossal chunk of rock and ice broke free at around 5,200 meters above sea level, triggering a devastating avalanche of debris and water towards the Nepal-Tibet border. The rapid retreat of glaciers in the region has made it clear that these natural wonders are no longer as stable as they once were. The thawing of permafrost may have played a significant role in destabilizing the Himalayan slopes, making them more susceptible to catastrophic events like this landslide. The impact of such disasters is not limited to the immediate destruction caused by the event itself but also has far-reaching consequences that can be seen in literature. As biologists and environmentalists continue to raise awareness about the effects of climate change on our planet's ecosystems. Rachel Carson's influential book "The Sea Around Us" published in 1951, highlighted the dynamic nature of our planet's boundaries, where land and sea have constantly interacted and transformed over millions of years. The impact of rising sea levels is becoming increasingly evident worldwide. Over the past three decades, the global average sea level has risen by approximately 10 centimeters (4 inches), a trend that began in 1993. This shift in landscape also affects the world depicted in books. For instance, a scene from Lore Segal's novel Half the Kingdom, published in 2013, takes place on a Brooklyn beach that could soon be underwater due to rising sea levels. The consequences of climate change are being explored in various works of literature. Philip Hoare's The Sea Inside, also from 2013, delves into coastal areas from England to Sri Lanka that may soon face submersion. Works of literature often remain unchanged despite the changing landscape. Instead, it is our understanding and interpretation that evolve as we read these stories across different eras and cultures. In Theodor Storm's novella, The Rider on the White Horse, published in 1888, a character named Hauke Haien uses his knowledge of geometry to construct dikes along Germany's North Sea coast. The narrative of literary works can be reinterpreted over time as new knowledge emerges. When Theodor Storm's novella was written, it described a coastline that was real at the time. However, today we know that coastlines are dynamic and constantly changing due to climate change. This shift in understanding has implications for how we read classic literature. We're not necessarily looking for hidden meanings or interpretations, but rather seeing familiar stories through a new lens. Texts that were once seen as realistic can now seem fantastical because they describe landscapes that no longer exist. Conversely, works of fantasy might start to seem more grounded in reality. This phenomenon is particularly relevant when it comes to descriptions of extreme environments like Antarctica, which was once considered an unattainable and inhospitable place but has since been explored by humans. The notion that books can predict the future or replace scientific disciplines is far-fetched. Instead, they serve as vessels for preserving human experiences and bridging timelines that span beyond individual lifetimes. Books capture landscapes in their original state, a snapshot of what once was. As the world undergoes transformations, these descriptions remain unchanged on the page. The shift occurs in how we interpret them, not in the physical content itself. The static nature of book descriptions belies the dynamic reality of climate change. articles.title: Nvidia Reports Financial Results Amid Investor Concerns
articles.summary: The company reported improved revenue growth forecasts and pushed back against speculation of price cuts, leading to a sharp rebound in its shares.
articles.content: Nvidia's board of directors and interim CEO Colette Kress have managed to stall the growing momentum of Jensen Huang supporters, at least temporarily. The company reported its latest financial results on Tuesday, which sparked a flurry of investor reactions. In a note to investors, Kress acknowledged that the situation was extraordinary, but expressed confidence in the team's ability to navigate it. Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board, took the lead in addressing investor concerns during an earnings conference call. He issued a clear warning that questions about ousted CEO Jensen Huang would not be entertained, and emphasized the board's commitment to its current direction. This stance was met with skepticism by some investors, who saw it as a sign of defiance rather than reassurance. Nvidia's shares initially fell in response to Jones' comments, but Kress quickly provided a much-needed boost to investor sentiment. The company raised its revenue growth forecast for fiscal 2028, which helped to alleviate concerns about its financial performance. Additionally, Kress pushed back against speculation that Nvidia might need to cut prices to stay competitive, stating that profit margins would recover in the long term. The market responded positively to these developments, with Nvidia's shares rebounding sharply by late Tuesday evening. The stock had gained almost 5% in after-hours trading, a significant turnaround from its earlier decline. While this brief respite may not have addressed the underlying issues surrounding Jensen Huang's departure, it has at least provided some breathing room for the company and its leadership team. The call's Q&A session had just begun when Nvidia dropped a bombshell: Ian Buck, VP and president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, would join Kress in answering analysts' questions. This was not a typical move for the company. Buck is a highly respected technologist who co-created CUDA, the software that gives Nvidia's chips their AI capabilities. Buck has spent over two decades at Nvidia, forging close relationships with its biggest customers. He is often mentioned as a potential successor to Jensen Huang in reports and analyses. Analysts were clearly taken by surprise when Buck was introduced on the call, and some saw it as an attempt to mitigate the impact of Huang's departure. The setup seemed almost perfect for Nvidia: the board had made it clear that Huang would not be returning, Kress had provided reassurances about the company's business prospects, and a respected internal leader was being presented to investors. But then Buck failed to deliver on his introduction, remaining eerily silent throughout the Q&A session. Despite the awkwardness of Buck's non-performance, analysts were waiting for someone to ask him a question. However, no one did, leaving many in the audience wondering what had just transpired and what it might mean for Nvidia's future. The unexpected silence from Nvidia's potential new CEO left many in the audience wondering about its implications for the company's future. Buck's reluctance to speak up during the leadership crisis at Nvidia was puzzling, especially considering his high profile and potential role as CEO of one of the world's leading tech companies. It seemed counterintuitive that someone being touted as a possible leader would remain tight-lipped when given the opportunity to address investors on Wall Street. The enigmatic silence surrounding Buck's intentions has sparked speculation about Nvidia's future direction under its current leadership or otherwise. In contrast, some powerful supporters of Huang have reaffirmed their confidence in his return to the company. Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke expressed his enthusiasm for Huang's comeback, stating that it was in everyone's best interest. Lutke also noted that a founder like Huang can never be truly replaced, and Ives agrees with this assessment. Tyler Sweatt, CEO of Second Front Systems, warned that failure to adapt will have catastrophic consequences, with a "growing realization" that inaction will be "existential in the near future". This stark warning came at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum, where Sweatt discussed the pressing need for change with Fortune's Allie Garfinkle. Despite a surge of investment in defense tech, the Pentagon has not kept pace, and investors are growing impatient. With venture money pouring in at record levels, pressure is mounting on defense tech companies to deliver results, leading Sweatt to predict that consolidation will be the next major trend in the industry. In fact, Shield AI, an autonomous weapon developer, has already begun this process, announcing plans to raise $2.5 billion to support its acquisition of Echodyne, a radar systems company, for a total value of $5.3 billion. This massive deal is just one example of the consolidation that Sweatt believes will sweep through the industry in the next six months. The Pentagon's slow and cumbersome approval processes, combined with outdated technology production lines, are major obstacles to getting new tech into the hands of troops quickly enough. Sweatt described the organization as an "Industrial Age entity stuck in a bygone era, plagued by big long bureaucracies. The Pentagon's weapon acquisition programs are facing severe delays, with an average time of over 12 years to deliver a capability, according to a Government Accountability Office report published in July. This prolonged timeframe is attributed to the organization's outdated bureaucracy, which hinders innovation and efficiency. In contrast, companies like Shield are pushing the boundaries of defense technology by developing autonomous systems that can fly alongside human-piloted aircraft using advanced software such as Hivemind. Shield's autonomous fighter jet is designed to be developed at an unprecedented pace, with the company expecting it to take less than two years from conception to first flight. However, with billions being poured into this space, it is now viewed as a rapidly growing and lucrative field. The increased investment is not solely driven by U.S. government spending, but also by other countries that are boosting their defense budgets. articles.title: Shift from Old English to Middle English Documented through Study
articles.summary: A recent study has shed new light on the transformation of language in the twelfth century.
articles.content: A major shift occurred in the English-speaking world in the twelfth century as Old English gave way to Middle English. The change was so significant that it has puzzled historians for centuries, but a recent study by Ph.D. candidate Amos van Baalen sheds new light on how this transformation took place. Van Baalen's research focuses on sermons written by the 11th-century abbot Ælfric, who was a highly influential figure in his time and whose texts were still being copied and circulated centuries after his death. Ælfric's writings are particularly valuable for studying the transition from Old English to Middle English because they represent a unique blend of both languages. "Old English resembles Dutch and German, and even Swedish to some extent," van Baalen explains, highlighting its distinct characteristics. Van Baalen chose Ælfric's sermons specifically because they demonstrate how written language continued to evolve long after spoken language had begun to change. The evolution of Old English was a gradual process that spanned centuries. As language continued to change over time, written records began to reflect these shifts. One key development in this period was the decline of final nasals in unstressed syllables. This phenomenon is particularly evident in the use of the dative case in the plural, which remained consistent across all types of nouns in Old English. The -um ending, for example, was a distinctive feature that allowed researchers to track changes in spoken language over time. Van Baalen's analysis focused on the transcription of this case ending by later copyists. By examining whether they used an -m or -n, he could determine if the loss of final nasals in unstressed syllables had also affected the written language. This approach enabled him to reconstruct the extent to which spoken and written English diverged. The study also looked at vocabulary used in sermons from this period. One finding was that English words were not frequently replaced by French or Old Norse variants, suggesting a remarkable degree of linguistic continuity. Instead, regional dialects and variants began to emerge in written records. As people started writing what they heard, their texts reflected the changing sounds and rhythms of spoken language. This is evident in the presence of many words still used in English today, which were likely borrowed from other languages during this period. The gradual shift towards a more modern English pronunciation is a complex process that involved numerous linguistic developments over several centuries. By examining written records from this time, researchers can gain insight into how spoken language continued to evolve and change. The decline of Old English as a written language is an intriguing phenomenon that has puzzled linguists for centuries. As Latin's influence waned in England around the 12th century, it may have allowed people to write in English more freely, reflecting how they actually spoke rather than adhering strictly to traditional norms. This shift could have been facilitated by the growing presence of Anglo-Norman French in England, which may have reduced the dominance of Latin and given writers greater flexibility. As a result, written records from this period offer a unique window into the evolution of spoken language, providing valuable insights into how English continued to change over time. articles.title: EU-ETS1 CO2 Emissions Projected to Remain Substantial by 2040
articles.summary: A new study suggests that current EU-ETS1 policies may not be enough to significantly reduce CO2 emissions in the coming decades.
articles.content: A new study by the Oeko-Institut has shed light on the extent of residual CO₂ emissions under the EU Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS1) in 2040 and 2050. The research, commissioned by Carbon Market Watch, reveals that current CO₂ emissions covered by the EU-ETS1 could be significantly reduced by 2040. According to the study's findings, installations covered by the EU-ETS1, including waste incineration, are still expected to emit substantial amounts of CO₂ in 2040. The estimated range for these emissions is between 159 and 231 million metric tons of CO₂. This figure highlights the considerable challenge that remains in reducing greenhouse gas emissions under the EU's current policies. While a large portion of these emissions could be avoided using existing technologies, some residual emissions are likely to persist due to limitations in today's technology outlook. The study suggests that a significant share of residual emissions can be attributed to the time required for transitioning to climate-friendly technologies and developing necessary infrastructure. The study highlights that a significant portion of residual emissions could be avoided through targeted support for industrial transformation. However, several factors contribute to emissions remaining in 2040, including limited capacity for transporting and storing CO2, slow rollout of infrastructure for hydrogen derivatives, and restricted availability of these energy carriers and feedstocks. Researchers emphasize the importance of access to low-cost renewable electricity, sustained innovation, and well-developed infrastructure in reducing avoidable emissions. The study's findings suggest that residual emissions in 2040 could be significantly lower than previously anticipated, with levels potentially reaching only around half of the proposed emissions cap by the European Commission under the EU Emissions Trading System. Industry experts stress that policymakers can set ambitious caps to drive progress toward phasing out fossil fuels and achieving European climate targets. The majority of long-term residual emissions are expected to come from specific sectors, including waste incineration, cement and lime production, metal production, and the glass and ceramics industries. The European Union's goal of climate neutrality by 2050 relies heavily on reducing long-term residual emissions to a minimum. This is crucial because removing an equivalent amount of CO₂ from the atmosphere would be necessary to balance out these remaining emissions. To minimize the economic and environmental costs associated with carbon dioxide removal, it is essential that efforts are made to reduce long-term residual emissions as much as possible in sectors like waste incineration, cement production, metal manufacturing, and glassmaking. The study, which spanned four nations and involved hundreds of dogs, highlights how little we know about the intricate dynamics between humans and their furry friends. A dog's gut microbiome is more than just a matter of how efficiently it breaks down food or how convenient it is for owners to clean up after them. The health of the microbiome has far-reaching implications for a dog's quality of life, with potential links to behavioral issues and immune system function. The study's findings underscore the importance of considering the interconnectedness between human lifestyles and canine health. By examining the dynamics at play in this unique relationship, researchers hope to gain a deeper understanding of how we can better support the well-being of our furry companions. The gut microbiome plays a vital role in a dog's overall health, breaking down complex dietary fibers and assisting with nutrient digestion and absorption. But it also houses a significant portion of their immune system, which needs to be balanced for optimal functioning. An imbalance in the gut microbiome can lead to various issues, including skin problems, food sensitivities, ear infections, and chronic conditions like inflammatory bowel disease. Additionally, an imbalanced microbiome can cause short-term problems such as diarrhea and nausea, affecting a dog's energy levels. Defining what constitutes a balanced or normal microbiome is a challenging task, even in humans. The concept of "normal may be subjective, and for dogs, it can vary significantly from one individual to another. Environmental factors, including where the dog lives and who they interact with, also play a crucial role in shaping their gut microbiome. Research has shown that certain microbiome species or overgrowths can have either positive or negative effects on canine health. The relationship between humans, dogs, food, and the environment is complex and interconnected. Human lifestyles, including dietary habits and exposure to antibiotics, can influence the microbiome of both individuals and their dogs. Previous studies have explored how community habits and culture affect human microbiomes, with differences observed in people who consume sourdough bread regularly versus those who do not. However, little attention has been given to the impact of human lifestyles on the gut health of dogs living within these communities. The study analyzed the gut microbiome of over 250 dogs from diverse geographic locations, including Nepal, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, and the United States. These canine companions varied in their living situations, ranging from forager to agrarian to pastoralist to urban to industrialized lifestyles. This spectrum refers to where dogs obtain their food - from wild sources to commercial diets. The researchers aimed to understand how human lifestyles impact the gut microbiome of our furry friends, considering that dogs span a broad range of living conditions. The team found that the way humans live indeed affects the microbiome of their pets. Consequently, the concept of a normal" microbiome for housed dogs may differ significantly from that of dogs living outdoors or in other environments. A summary of the study highlights its significance: Domestic dogs are closely tied to human lives, yet surprisingly little is known about how their gut microbiomes vary outside of industrialized pet populations. This research demonstrates that lifestyle changes associated with industrialization not only impact human microbiomes but also influence the gut microbial communities of animals living alongside humans. The study's findings suggest that shared environments can impose similar pressures on the gut bacterial communities of both humans and dogs, while each host maintains a unique microbial identity. This implies that the gut health of dogs is closely linked to their environment and human lifestyle, challenging the idea of a single standard healthy microbiome for all housed dogs. The notion that dogs share a uniform gut microbiome has been challenged by research suggesting that ecological conditions play a significant role in shaping their microbial communities. This discovery underscores the importance of expanding microbiome studies beyond industrialized environments to gain a deeper understanding of how lifestyle transitions have impacted canine gut health. The findings indicate that household pets harbor distinct microbial profiles compared to dogs living in other ecosystems, which has important implications for establishing reference microbiomes and interpreting microbiome-based assessments of dog health. Moreover, the study suggests that factors influencing human lifestyles, such as consuming contaminated food or poor sleep habits, may also affect the gut microbiome of canines. The research revealed that while canine and human microbiomes exhibit similar shifts in response to lifestyle changes, they are not identical, with some differences attributed to species-specific characteristics, country of residence, and environmental factors like weather patterns and temperatures. The study found that industrialization has a profound impact on the gut microbiome of domestic dogs. This restructuring is not limited to specific regions or breeds, but rather appears to be a widespread phenomenon affecting dogs globally. Industrialization leads to changes in the types and proportions of microbes present in dog guts, with some species becoming more dominant while others decline. While these shifts are similar to those observed in human microbiomes, there are notable differences between the two that may be due to species-specific characteristics or country of origin. articles.title: Nvidia Chairperson Harvey Jones Confirms No Return for Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia's chairperson Harvey Jones closed the door on speculation about Jensen Huang's potential return to the company during its first earnings call without him at the helm.
articles.content: Nvidia's chairperson Harvey Jones closed the door on speculation about Jensen Huang's potential return to the company during its first earnings call without him at the helm. The board of directors has made it clear that they do not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, with Jones stating that "we will not be addressing or taking questions on today's call regarding the circumstances of Jensen's resignation and the ongoing investigation". This ruling out of discussion about why Huang left has been met with a lack of inquiry from analysts, with none of the eight present on the call asking follow-up questions. The absence of questions about Huang's departure and subsequent investigation was notable, given that Nvidia had just reported a significant beating of Wall Street estimates in quarterly revenue. The company posted $115.8 billion in revenue, a staggering figure that saw its stock rise nearly 5% in after-hours trading to around $163 per share. Jones provided some insight into Huang's resignation during the call, stating that he "voluntarily resigned on November 12 due to personal behavior that was inconsistent with Nvidia's code of conduct and cultural norms. The board accepted his resignation unanimously, Jones noted, adding that they have since hired a search firm to consider both internal and external candidates for the top role. The call with analysts had a one-question limit, but Bank of America's Vivek Arya managed to squeeze in a question about talent retention and leadership transition. Interim CEO Colette Kress responded that among employees, there is a mix of opinions on the situation. From a business perspective, it appears that everything is proceeding as usual, according to Kress. Analysts also asked about margins, vendor financing, and next year's outlook during the call. Their questions were focused on the company's financial health and future prospects. However, one question was noticeably absent from the discussion: the issue of customers billed in Singapore. According to Nvidia's 10-Q filing, $10.2 billion in sales, representing 22% of its revenue, came from these customers in the quarter that ended July 2025. It is worth noting that the majority of this revenue, over 99%, was attributed to orders from U.S.-based customers. The company explained in its filing that customers use Singapore for centralized invoicing purposes, while their products are often shipped elsewhere. The discrepancy between the billing location and the actual shipping destination raises questions about the nature of these transactions and how they fit into Nvidia's business operations. Nvidia's shift to reporting revenue by customer headquarters location has eliminated Singapore as a separate line item, providing a new perspective on its geographic revenue profile. A criminal investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company, is being led jointly by the Commerce and Justice departments, which had begun probing the firm in 2024. The investigation centers around allegations that Megaspeed helped Nvidia export high-end technology to China. According to reports, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on a no sell" list in June 2025. The Wall Street Journal has revealed that the Securities and Exchange Commission is launching a separate civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures have been misleading investors. This development adds another layer of scrutiny for the company as it navigates the complex landscape surrounding its business dealings with China. Nvidia has announced that licensed Hopper data center chip sales to China generated $2.4 billion in revenue during the last quarter, but the company is no longer shipping these products to the country. The firm's forecast for the next quarter assumes zero data center compute revenue from China, indicating a significant shift in its business strategy. Nvidia's chairwoman has emphasized that the company will carefully examine new export rules from the Commerce Department, which impose stricter controls on access to advanced chips via other countries. The firm is poised to maintain strong performance due to an ongoing mismatch between demand and supply, despite these increased regulatory hurdles. Meanwhile, Nvidia has upgraded its revenue growth forecast for fiscal 2028 to around 75%, up from a previous estimate of 70%. This revised projection suggests the company remains confident in its prospects despite the challenging export environment. Nvidia's customer base is also undergoing significant changes, with frontier AI labs expected to account for approximately 15% of the company's data center revenue this year. The firm will soon release its first regional revenue breakdown since Jensen Huang's exit as CEO, which is scheduled to be included in its upcoming 10-Q filing. As part of ongoing investigations, Huang and general counsel Tim Teter have agreed to provide transcribed interviews with three House committees. With Pattinson at the helm, it's possible to envision a Bond who is not just a brooding figure but also someone with a playful edge. Televisions, often placed in bedrooms for convenience, have been singled out as a culprit by some interior experts. According to Rayman Boozer, TVs can be visually distracting even when turned off. Boozer points out that the typically black color of televisions can clash with most bedroom decor themes. Unless a specific design aesthetic incorporates black and white or another bold combination, the TV's appearance can be jarring in an otherwise peaceful space. In contrast, Boozer acknowledges that watching TV in bed is not inherently wrong. Other designers concur on the importance of maintaining separate spaces for work and rest. Avoiding a desk or work area in your bedroom is Beth Diana Smith's advice, aimed at promoting a clear distinction between these two essential activities. Clear surfaces and smart storage solutions are key to maintaining organization in the bedroom, according to Maya's advice. Clutter can have a significant impact on sleep quality, making it essential to keep surfaces clear of unnecessary items. By incorporating storage solutions that are both functional and aesthetically pleasing, individuals can create a calm and relaxing environment. Bright colors can stimulate energy and make relaxation more difficult, which is why designer Debbie Mathews recommends avoiding bold hues in the bedroom. Interior designer Lorna Gross agrees, advising against using bright versions of red, orange, and yellow paint. These colors are often associated with anxiety and arguments, making them less than ideal for a space where rest and rejuvenation take place. Large or intricately designed mirrors can be problematic in the bedroom, as they can create the illusion of a smaller space or even stimulate anxiety, according to Alexa Larson, co-founder of Dwellify. While mirrors can enhance a room's light and spaciousness, it's essential to exercise caution when selecting mirror sizes and designs for the bedroom. Mirrors can greatly impact a bedroom's ambiance, but their placement is crucial to avoid overwhelming the space. Placing sizable mirrors directly across from the bed can create an unsettling atmosphere that disrupts the room's balance. To maintain a serene environment, electrical clutter should be kept at bay. Designer Larson recommends concealing cables behind furniture or investing in wireless charging options to prevent exposed wires from detracting from the bedroom's ambiance. Exposed wires not only compromise the space's tidiness but also pose a safety risk if tangled or overloaded. Proper lighting is essential for creating a cozy atmosphere, and designers agree that harsh single-source lighting can make the room feel cold and uninviting. Instead of relying on a single light source, aim for a mix of ambient, task, and accent lighting to set the mood and aid in navigation. When designing a bedroom, it's essential to consider the overall atmosphere and ambiance that will promote relaxation and restful sleep. Soft, layered lighting can create a warm and inviting space perfect for unwinding after a long day. According to designer Amber Guyton of Blessed Little Bungalow, electronics have no place in the bedroom as they can be major distractions and disrupt sleep patterns. The absence of electronic devices is crucial in creating an environment conducive to relaxation and rejuvenation. In addition to avoiding electronics, designers also recommend keeping furniture at uniform heights and avoiding clutter by storing personal items out of sight, such as kids' toys, which should ideally be kept out of the primary bedroom altogether. articles.title: Nationwide Ground Stop Causes Disruptions and Delays in US Air Travel
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration's request for $50 billion in new funding has been met with skepticism from lawmakers, who question whether such a large sum is justified.
articles.content: Air travel in the US has been severely disrupted following a nationwide ground stop that caused widespread delays and cancellations for thousands of flights on Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration is seeking $50 billion in new funding to address the crisis, a significant increase from its initial request of $30 billion. The sudden surge in funding demand was outlined in a letter signed by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who has been criticized for his handling of the situation. Despite calls for accountability, Duffy has refused to apologize or accept responsibility for the failure, instead blaming predecessors and Congress. He has publicly rebuked Congress for its role in the crisis. In a closed-door briefing with Senate Republicans on Tuesday, Duffy faced intense questioning from multiple senators who "yelled at him during the meeting, according to an individual present but not authorized to speak publicly about the discussion. The tension was palpable as Senate Republican leaders and Duffy opted to hold separate news conferences after the briefing. A $50 billion price tag for fixing air travel issues has sparked heated debate on Capitol Hill, with some lawmakers questioning whether such a large sum is justified. The proposal, put forth by Rep. Sean Duffy, was met with skepticism and frustration from Democrats who felt he failed to provide sufficient justification for the massive funding request. Duffy's decision to meet only with Republican colleagues on Tuesday has added fuel to the fire, with many arguing that bipartisan support is essential in addressing such a critical issue. The regular government funding process requires cooperation from both parties, yet Duffy chose not to involve Democrats in his initial discussions. Democrats are now calling for a more detailed explanation of how the proposed funds would be allocated and what specific upgrades they would cover. Some have expressed concern that the $12 billion already allocated for air traffic control has yet to be fully utilized, making it unclear why an additional $50 billion is necessary. Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii is closely watching the air travel funding debate as he prepares to take on a key leadership role in the Senate. As majority whip and a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Schatz will be instrumental in shaping the final bill. The looming deadline of December 11 adds an extra layer of urgency to the negotiations. If Congress fails to reach a deal by then, it could trigger another government shutdown, which would have far-reaching consequences for various sectors. Lawmakers are now weighing their options on how to proceed with funding the government. One possibility is that Republicans might push through a party-line reconciliation" bill to approve military funding without needing Democratic support. However, Democrats are unlikely to agree to additional military funds unless there's progress on ending the war in Iran. Sean Duffy's proposal to allocate $50 billion to address air travel issues was met with skepticism in Congress on Tuesday. He expressed his willingness to work with Democrats to pass the funds, but chose to meet exclusively with Republicans. Duffy emphasized that he has a good relationship with Democratic lawmakers and has spent considerable time discussing the issue with them over the phone. When asked by reporters about his decision to only meet with Republicans, he noted that he is not trying to dictate how Democrats conduct their work. articles.title: Trends in Travel Highlight Shift Towards Immersive Culinary Experiences
articles.summary: A series of expert-led discussions shed light on the latest trends in immersive culinary experiences and multigenerational travel.
articles.content: Our Points of View Summit kicked off with a series of expert-led discussions that shed light on the latest trends in travel. The event featured an array of panels and breakouts where our team of specialists shared their insights on various topics. Travelers are increasingly seeking out immersive culinary experiences, and our summit provided a platform for experts to share their knowledge on this subject. Senior features editor Megan Spurrell and editorial assistant Skyli Alvarez led a discussion on the evolution of food travel, from traditional cooking classes to more adventurous pursuits like foraging. The interest in authentic food moments is clear, but defining what constitutes authenticity can be a challenge. According to Omolola Campbell, executive producer of The Spirit We Move With, an intimate understanding of local culture and traditions is essential to creating meaningful culinary experiences. Campbell shared the significance of okra in Gullah cuisine, explaining that its use in traditional dishes is deeply rooted in the history of West African slaves who were brought to South Carolina. "Taking a cooking class is much different than getting it from a local chef," she said, highlighting the importance of stories and context in understanding the cultural significance of food. The summit also explored the changing dynamics of multigenerational travel, with our specialists discussing the ways in which families are choosing to spend their vacations together. The rise of all-inclusive stays has been particularly notable in recent years, offering a convenient and stress-free option for travelers seeking a hassle-free getaway. As we continue to explore the latest trends in travel, one thing is clear: today's travelers crave experiences that go beyond mere sightseeing. They seek out immersive, authentic moments that allow them to connect with local cultures and traditions. Travelers today are seeking unique experiences that allow them to connect with local cultures and traditions in an authentic way. The traditional notion of multigenerational travel is evolving as grandparents join trips at older ages, often alongside younger family members who choose the destinations. This shift has significant implications for trip designers, who must now cater to a wide range of activity levels and exertion needs within one itinerary. To accommodate this diverse group, it's recommended that families have multiple options available on any given day, allowing younger travelers to pursue their interests while still coming together for shared experiences. Mealtimes and afternoon activities are ideal opportunities for family members to reunite, and boat and yacht experiences can be particularly beneficial in fostering a sense of togetherness among family members. The luxury travel industry's definition of opulence is undergoing a significant shift, according to experts who gathered at our recent summit. Luxury, Virgi Schiffino Kennedy, managing partner at Lux Voyage, explained, "is being able to pass on meaning to kids [and] exposing families to the broader world and its cultures," highlighting its intangible appeal. This perspective emphasizes the importance of creating lasting memories and experiences for future generations. A key demographic driving this shift is Gen Z and Millennials, who are more inclined to spend on travel but want transparency about where their money goes, Thomas Robinson, MR at Dehouche, noted. As a result, travelers are seeking authentic and immersive experiences that align with their values. The trend of family members traveling together is also evolving, with 30- and 40-somethings increasingly treating their parents to vacations, rather than the other way around. Milestone birthdays and anniversaries are driving clients to book trips, according to Harnal's experience. As the Euro summer season approaches, concerns about overtourism, price inflation, and rising temperatures are top of mind for travelers. Director of special projects Lale Arikoglu and commerce editor Meaghan Kenny opened the floor for our specialists to weigh in on these pressing issues. Some experts recommend exploring Switzerland as an alternative to popular destinations like the Dolomites, where crowds can be overwhelming. Brian Dore, owner of CIU Travel, suggested considering one-day hiking trails or "soft adventure travel in Switzerland, combining a lake or city destination with outdoor activities for three-to-four days. For families looking for a unique experience, destinations like Umbria in Italy offer an abundance of festivals and craft activities perfect for kids to enjoy. Alternatively, Austria, Ireland, or Croatia provide excellent options for those seeking a mix of culture and outdoor adventure. Traveling during the shoulder season can be beneficial, as May is now being recommended over August for those who prefer milder weather on their European vacations. When planning a trip to France, flying into Paris or Nice allows visitors to easily explore the countryside or lesser-known Atlantic Coast regions. Before embarking on any journey, it's essential to check the local climate conditions in advance to ensure a comfortable and enjoyable experience. The demand for travel to Asia continues to rise, with Mei Zhang, chairman and founder at WildChina, highlighting the increasing popularity of destinations across the continent. As the travel industry continues to evolve, sporting events, music festivals, and art fairs are becoming major draws for travelers. These high-demand events often require bundled purchases due to limited availability of individual tickets, as seen at Pink's performance at The Sphere, which necessitates a Venetian hotel package. The lack of stringent legal protections in the US enables extreme ticket scalping for stadium concerts, making domestic events increasingly unaffordable for many. This has created a challenge for travel advisors like Stephanie Malakie, founder of Empress Travel Club, who struggle to filter options and find suitable experiences for clients amidst the numerous events and providers. To navigate this issue, specialists recommend curating the surrounding experience or tapping into niche experiential travel opportunities, such as watching sports teams play in unique locations like London's Wembley Stadium. Cultural milestones like attending European Christmas markets or Vatican City trips featuring Papal Blessings can also be paired with entertainment options for a more immersive experience. Set-jetting to filming locations is another trend gaining traction, offering value without the hassle of peak-event ticketing, according to Mei Zhang's observations. This approach allows travelers to explore new destinations and tap into their interests in a more relaxed manner. The great outdoors has become a major focus in travel, with many seeking nature-based wellness experiences. However, experts warn that the trend for dumbphone fantasies", disconnecting from technology and immersing oneself in natural settings, may be less achievable than anticipated due to logistical challenges and limited availability of such experiences. Guests at the Points of View Summit are looking for a balance between technology access and natural immersion, but not necessarily a complete digital detox. According to Kate Doty, trip designer at Geographic Expeditions, Wi-Fi is still a must-have for emergency purposes, with no guest requesting a full digital detox. This suggests that while travelers want to disconnect from the digital world, they also value having some level of connectivity available. To reduce dependency on phones, services like on-board photographers can be offered, allowing guests to capture memories without needing their own devices. The trend towards glamping is also still strong, with travelers seeking luxury and nature in equal measure. This desire for both comfort and immersion is driving the demand for unique experiences that combine these two elements. By reframing a destination's seasons and characteristics, it's possible to find value in what might otherwise be seen as drawbacks. For example, a rainy season can bring lush greenery and other benefits that make a trip more enjoyable. By embracing this unpredictability and incorporating it into travel plans, travelers can have a more authentic and engaging experience, learning something new with each visit. articles.title: Breakthrough in Supercomputer Workflow Accelerates Protein Structure Prediction
articles.summary: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory have developed an optimized computing workflow that enables the generation of predicted protein structures at an unprecedented rate.
articles.content: A breakthrough in supercomputer workflow has enabled researchers to accelerate the generation of predicted protein structures at an unprecedented rate. This achievement, led by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), promises to revolutionize various fields including drug discovery and biological research. The optimized computing workflow is part of a project called ElMerFold, which leverages advanced biomolecular models for improved accuracy. By generating millions of predicted protein structures as training data, the team aims to enhance these models' capabilities. Researchers from LLNL collaborated with experts at AMD and Columbia University to push the limits of high-performance computing on El Capitan, a machine capable of exascale operations. The result was astonishing: over 10,700 predicted protein structures per second were generated across thousands of accelerated processing units. The team's achievement has earned them a spot among finalists for the prestigious ACM Gordon Bell Prize, with the winner to be announced next month at the SC26 conference in Chicago. The project's scope extended beyond the realm of protein folding, as it aimed to develop new capabilities for large-scale superintelligence research and infrastructure. According to Brian Van Essen, this collaboration offered a unique chance to tackle pressing challenges in biology and machine learning workflows for high-performance computing. Proteins play a crucial role in nearly every biological process, and understanding their three-dimensional structures is essential for determining how they function and interact with other molecules. The experimental determination of protein structures is often expensive and time-consuming, limiting the amount of available data for developing computational prediction models. Researchers acknowledge that this shortage of real data hinders the training of state-of-the-art protein structure prediction models. Nikoli Dryden notes that acquiring new experimental structures requires significant resources in terms of time, expense, and effort. As a result, researchers must supplement these limited data with synthetic information to aid their predictions. Existing prediction models are generating synthetic protein structures to train new models in a process called distillation. This approach is crucial for producing large data sets required by modern biomolecular models, which can be computationally expensive and sometimes costlier than the models themselves. The resulting data set is being used to enhance OpenFold3's ability to predict complex molecular interactions, particularly those between antibodies and antigens they recognize. According to Mohammed AlQuraishi, a collaborator on the ElMerFold project, this distillation set improves OpenFold3 performance by refining its understanding of protein structure biophysics. Understanding how antibodies bind to biological targets is essential for developing therapeutics against infectious diseases, and predicting drug-protein interactions could accelerate early-stage drug discovery. To achieve the desired performance level, the research team had to thoroughly optimize both the prediction software and the underlying computing infrastructure. This involved leveraging the capabilities of El Capitan's processors by scaling the workflow across nearly its entire system. The researchers exploited the unique features of AMD's MI300A APUs, which integrate CPUs and GPUs with shared high-bandwidth memory, thereby reducing unnecessary data transfers and enhancing computational efficiency. By doing so, they were able to streamline the computing process and minimize delays. Specialized components were developed to fine-tune El Capitan's processors, including optimized computational kernels, advanced memory management strategies, and innovative scheduling techniques. This allowed the system to operate at peak performance levels without compromising its processing capacity. To further enhance efficiency, the team implemented persistent inference servers, eliminating the need for repeated model loading, and utilized El Capitan's Rabbit near-node storage system from HPE for rapid data access. Throughout this optimization process, the researchers collaborated closely with Columbia University experts in protein folding to ensure that performance gains did not come at the expense of prediction accuracy. The team also made significant contributions to compiler frameworks such as DaCe, enabling the generation of highly optimized computations tailored to the MI300A architecture. This expertise could potentially benefit other applications and programs within the lab, as expressed by LLNL computer scientist Tal Ben-Nun: "We went as far as writing machine-level instructions to maximize the performance of the system." The optimization of ElMerFold has led to significant advancements in protein-structure prediction, thanks to its ability to harness the power of El Capitan's AMD Instinct MI300A architecture and AMD ROCm software. This achievement is particularly noteworthy given the importance of exascale systems in accelerating the creation of training data for scientific models. As a result, researchers can now generate larger and more detailed datasets, opening up new avenues of inquiry across various disciplines such as materials science, chemistry, and physics. The implications of ElMerFold extend beyond molecular biology to LLNL's national security mission, where limited training data poses a significant challenge. This scarcity of data hinders the development of computational models for stockpile modernization and other applications in the NNSA mission space. To address this challenge, researchers are exploring the use of scientifically grounded synthetic training data, which ElMerFold has shown to be an effective approach. By doing so, scientists can better interpret and understand rare or anomalous events, a crucial aspect of their work in national security missions. The ElMerFold data set has been made accessible to researchers worldwide, enabling them to create new scientific models using the predictions. This move is expected to foster further development of protein-structure prediction methods. To enhance its capabilities, the team aims to generate a wider range of training data sets, including those for predicting complex proteins composed of multiple interacting molecules. The inclusion of these diverse datasets will provide researchers with more robust tools for their work. The researchers plan to integrate the latest OpenFold3 model into the ElMerFold workflow, ultimately refining the core scalable inference framework to make it adaptable to various scientific workloads. articles.title: Nvidia Quarterly Earnings Report Set for Release
articles.summary: The chipmaker is set to release its quarterly earnings report on Tuesday, providing a glimpse into its financial health after a tumultuous period.
articles.content: Nvidia's quarterly earnings report is set to be released on Tuesday, providing a glimpse into the company's financial health after a tumultuous period. The chipmaker has seen its stock price plummet 35% from its peak last month, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market value and sparking widespread concern among investors. The AI industry, which Nvidia is at the forefront of, is now under scrutiny as the company struggles to reassure investors. If Nvidia fails to deliver a convincing earnings report, it could have far-reaching consequences for the entire sector, potentially dragging other companies down with it. The stakes are high, and investors are anxiously waiting for news. Jensen Huang's sudden departure from the CEO position has left a power vacuum at Nvidia, which he founded. In a statement, Huang pledged to return as CEO if the board of directors deemed it in the best interest of shareholders and the country. However, despite calls from influential figures including President Donald Trump, the board has yet to make a decision. The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia over allegations that the company misled investors. This probe adds to the growing list of concerns surrounding the chipmaker's financials and business practices. The investigation is also fueling fears about potential national security implications arising from Nvidia's involvement in illegal export deals. Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief and interim CEO, will be under intense scrutiny as she attempts to convince investors that the company is on a stable trajectory. Market confidence has been shaken by supply chain backlogs for advanced chips and servers, which are critical components of AI infrastructure and large language models. Nvidia's strategic maneuvering under Huang has made it a crucial player for AI labs and data centers, not just by supplying hardware but also by providing financial backing through various means. Critics have raised concerns that Nvidia's circular financing schemes, which involve funding hyperscalers like Meta or Microsoft in exchange for product purchases, may have contributed to the inflated AI bubble. These arrangements have been a source of contention among executives, including Kress. Nvidia is reportedly reassessing its involvement in high-risk AI financial deals, such as investments in OpenAI and infrastructure companies like Lambda. This shift comes after scaling back financing for a $250 billion OpenAI data center deal, which was a significant undertaking. The tech industry may face challenges if Nvidia continues to distance itself from GPU commitments. The semiconductor production landscape is highly specialized, dominated by a few key players, making supply chain disruptions potentially far-reaching and affecting consumer electronics and cloud services. Nvidia's handling of outstanding deals inked under Huang's leadership will be closely watched during the earnings call, particularly since the company can no longer rely on revenue from certain export arrangements. Nvidia's dominance in the market for data center hardware and AI model training has led to a situation where demand far outstrips supply. The shortage of RAM and high-bandwidth memory is particularly problematic as it slows down production and drives up costs for cloud companies and other buyers. To mitigate this issue, Nvidia has invested heavily in securing future memory supplies, but the effort may not be enough to alleviate the bottleneck. Meanwhile, the controversy surrounding Huang's personal life has created new challenges for the company. His ties to a Chinese executive linked to Megaspeed have raised questions about the integrity of the supply chain. The company's reliance on third-party countries to divert advanced chips to China has been identified as a significant issue by investment research firm Culper, which estimates that up to one-fifth of Nvidia's compute revenues in fiscal year 2026 came from this process. The AI buildout relies heavily on hardware companies like Nvidia, making them vulnerable to industry-wide downturns in investor confidence. If Nvidia's earnings call indicates strong growth, it could boost stocks and funds focused on technology, potentially leading to a surge in the value of individual retirement accounts and 401(k)s. Major funds and indices are dominated by a handful of big tech companies, often referred to as the Magnificent Seven. These firms account for nearly one-third of the S&P 500 index and have significant exposure to AI-related stocks. This means that investors who hold these companies through index funds may be indirectly affected by fluctuations in Nvidia's stock price. The impact of an AI selloff could extend beyond individual investors, potentially affecting retirement balances even for those who don't own Nvidia shares directly. The Magnificent Seven are particularly vulnerable to AI stock swings, with their share prices often closely tied to the performance of companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Alphabet's recent experience serves as a stark reminder that even top tech firms can be affected by market fluctuations triggered by Nvidia news. Intel and CoreWeave, both heavily focused on AI infrastructure, have also seen their share prices decline in response to growing concerns over AI dangers. As the debate around AI risks intensifies, companies like Nvidia are facing increased scrutiny over their role in the development of artificial general intelligence. The company's CEO has been a prominent advocate for AI, framing it as an economic and national-security imperative, but recent developments have raised questions about the pace and scope of AI advancements. The recent controversies surrounding Huang's leadership have added to the growing unease about the pace and scope of AI advancements in the US. As Nvidia prepares for its earnings call, the tech industry is bracing itself for a potential backlash against data centers and large-scale AI projects, which have become increasingly unpopular among politicians and voters. Democrats are pushing for stricter regulations on the AI industry, including laws to prevent an industry bailout if a bubble were to burst. This shift in public opinion has caught many in the industry off guard. The bipartisan calls for Huang to testify before Congress have highlighted concerns about Nvidia's dealings with China and potential export loopholes. Some politicians are also investigating high-ranking officials at US intelligence and the Commerce Department, accusing them of failing to act on knowledge of Nvidia's China-related deals. This scrutiny is likely to continue in the coming months. Kress may be able to distance herself from some of Nvidia's riskiest ventures, but her predecessor's relationships have left a lasting impact on the company's national security implications. The investigation into these dealings has opened up a Pandora's box that no CEO can easily close. The federal government's response to these developments is likely to be slow and cumbersome, but there is an increasing momentum towards investigating the major players in the AI industry. This will undoubtedly have a chilling effect on investor hype and put pressure on companies like Nvidia to re-evaluate their priorities.
